races.title: State Senate, District 1
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Jerry Tillett
cands.bio: Retired North Carolina Senior Resident Superior Court Judge (appointed 1993, over 30 years on the bench). Earlier a Dare County attorney and Chief of Staff and Chief Legal Counsel to the NC Senate President Pro Tempore. Business owner. Republican. Holds the NC Senate District 1 seat from 2026.

endorsements.text: Endorsed in the 2026 primary by NC Rep. Keith Kidwell (House District 79), Dare County Commissioner Carson Creef, and Dare County attorney Dan Merrell, according to the campaign website. Ballotpedia did not identify endorsements for him in this election.
In his 2010 judicial race, which was unopposed, he was endorsed by the North Carolina Democratic Party, according to Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: His birthplace and the year he moved to North Carolina are not stated in the pages we could read. We found no legislative record for him other than his appointment to the seat, and no bills he sponsored. We found no stated positions or actions on data centers, homestead taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration or H-1B, school choice, abortion, or clean-money pledges. His campaign site lists priorities of law and order, free enterprise, economic prosperity, quality of life and open debate, but these are general and do not address those issues. A campaign press release about his support for the Second Amendment was cut off on the page we read, so we left it out. His Ballotpedia survey answers were brief. His campaign biography page was cut off partway through, so some of his teaching and other background may be missing. We found no news coverage or documented controversies about him, and no foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign biography says he grew up on the Outer Banks of North Carolina and later practiced law in Dare County, but it does not give his birthplace.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Lawyer and partner in a Dare County firm. Chief of Staff and Chief Legal Counsel to the NC Senate President Pro Tempore. Superior Court judge from 1993 to 2025, including Senior Resident Judge of the First Judicial District. Owner of several businesses, including water-sports, home-building and rental operations.
qual.why: He has a long legal career, staff experience on legislation and committees in the state Senate, and business ownership, which fits the middle-to-upper range. He has not held a legislative seat before, so he does not reach the top band. Most of this comes from his own campaign biography.

cands.name: Melissa Zehner
cands.bio: Democratic nominee for North Carolina Senate District 1. Graduated from Randolph-Macon Woman's College and held management positions in Minor League Baseball. Later became a stay-at-home parent. Mother of two children in public schools. No elected office held.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists recommendations from several Sway voting groups, including NC Public School Champions, Fair Map Fight Club, People Over Politics and Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress. These are voter-guide groups, not organizations or officeholders.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Melissa Zehner was born or when she moved to North Carolina. Her campaign site says she was raised in Farmville, Virginia, and now lives on the Outer Banks. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, and we found no detailed policy statements on data centers, development, property taxes, land ownership, immigration, policing, guns or abortion. We found no documented actions in office, since she has held none. We found no news coverage or controversies about her, and no public statements on land use or development.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
